images.title: Comparing angles by overlapping
images.purpose: Two angles are compared by placing one on the other with the joints together; the wider opening is the larger angle.
images.composition: Two arm pairs side by side with wide space between them, plenty of white space around.
images.exact_structure: Left: one narrow angle of two straight arms in teal #0072B2 with a small arc. Right: one wider angle of two straight arms in amber #E69F00 with a small arc. Both pairs have arms of exactly the same length and a round dot at the joint. Exactly 2 angles, 2 joints, 2 arcs.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any of the following: arm pairs of different lengths
images.takeaway: Put the joints together and the wider opening is the larger angle.
images.description: Two same-length arm pairs: a narrow teal angle and a wide amber angle, each with a small arc at the joint.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the joint, then at the opening that is wider.

image_decisions.why: Comparing two angles by overlapping is a picture idea; one clean image of a narrow and a wide opening carries it.
